narrative: Frequent operational bugs across dashboards, report builder, and admin/seats are mostly fixed within a day or two, but several recur: the report-builder section-deletion bug returns "on a different template" the day after being marked fixed, and the seat-limit issue draws three messages in one week ("third message on the same thing this week"). Support is fast but the recurrence pattern is wearing the customer down, most visibly in the dense October cluster.

Routine setup questions gave way to a two-week unresolved connector failure that made the team stop trusting the data ("our reporting team has effectively stopped using the connector data because it's too unreliable. Please escalate"), followed immediately by dashboards going down over year-end close with "no resolution" from support. Both of the two most recent tickets end unresolved, and the trajectory is sharply downward with real business impact at stake.

competitor_mentions.quote: Migrating our old Storsund BI report templates over - is there a way to import layout definitions, or do we need to rebuild everything from scratch in the builder?

narrative: Three straightforward onboarding questions over several months, all resolved within days, with a passing reference to migrating away from a legacy tool rather than any live comparison shopping. No friction of any kind visible in the text.

A rough four months of recurring bugs (settings not persisting across dashboards and report builder, a connector fix that itself widened access scope, then daily connector failures the customer called "worse than ever") culminated in a demand for "a thorough review of what's happening, not another patch." The account settled by August: the large-export bug is still only worked around ("adds about 20 minutes to our month-end close") but the tone turns calm and collaborative, with the customer offering to test a real fix.

High-frequency but low-severity bug reports across every module for a year, nearly all fixed within one to two days; recurring bug types (report builder save errors, permission resets) reflect a genuinely glitchy product, but each specific incident closes without a confirmed later recurrence. Tone stays matter-of-fact throughout, including the most recent tickets, with no sign of rising anger or shrinking engagement.
A single ticket about a missed scheduled export, resolved slowly (11 days) but with a calm, factual tone throughout. Too sparse to show a pattern, and nothing concerning in what is there.

A heavy, active account generating incident tickets across every module over 18 months (blank dashboards, alert failures, API errors, connector outages), but resolution is consistently fast (mostly one to two days) and tone never exceeds routine urgency ("please prioritise," "obviously"). The one true recurrence, an ERP connector outage a year apart, gets flagged for root cause ("check if there's a recurring cause rather than treating each outage separately") without any expression of lost patience.

A months-long export-scheduler failure survived two supposed fixes ("the fix applied in December worked for about three weeks. It's broken again in the same way") and led to an explicit escalation request in February 2025 ("can someone senior look at it?"), compounded by an unannounced API schema change that broke production and was never confirmed resolved ("these things add up"). The most recent ticket, in March, is markedly calmer and purely informational, suggesting some recovery, but the API-stability complaint has no documented closure.

Only three tickets across roughly a year, but the most recent is the quiet-withdrawal pattern in its purest form: an alert-digest bug "first flagged... the better part of a year ago" that the customer has simply routed around with a manual Monday Excel check, explicitly saying "there's no pressure to prioritise this" and framing the message as "just wanted it on file." Long silence plus a shrinking ask plus an entrenched workaround is a quiet risk signal, not a healthy low-volume account.

A steady stream of how-to questions over a year with no bug reports, calm tone throughout, and one explicit positive follow-up confirming a feature is "working well, saved us a fair amount of setup time." A textbook healthy account.

A serious five-month connector/API reliability crisis drove a formal escalation demanding a named owner and timeline ("I'd like this formally escalated... I need to speak to someone who can commit to a fix and a timeline"). It was followed by genuine resolution: the customer confirms in September "the connector has held steady for a full month... the longest stable stretch we've had since last November" and thanks the team, with subsequent tickets calm, appreciative, and low-stakes through October. This is the anger-to-recovery arc, not an active risk.

A short, calm sequence around setting up multi-subsidiary consolidated reporting; the original request to merge data sources correctly is marked unresolved and never explicitly confirmed fixed even after a related connector question is answered, leaving the core ask an open thread. Tone is cooperative throughout with no frustration.

Four well-spaced, professional setup questions (on-premise connector, export timezone, post-migration connector reconfiguration, multi-condition alerts) all resolved without complaint. A textbook healthy implementation-phase account.

A dense cluster of four simultaneous failures in November 2024 ("three things broken in two days is not normal for us") drew a demand for a call rather than another ticket ("at this point I'd like a call, not just a ticket queue"); the same API and connector faults then recur in March and May 2025 with the customer explicitly noting the repetition ("same symptom as November", "check whether whatever caused that has come back") and asking for a permanent fix "instead of a restart each time." Unlike similar accounts in this batch, there is no confirming calm period afterward — the data ends mid-complaint.
A single informational question about API rate limits ahead of a planned polling increase, resolved without issue. No risk signal in the text.

Alerts tied to GL data went silent for months without the customer noticing until a known budget breach failed to fire ("we know we breached two budget thresholds" with nothing triggered), and a later dashboard bug excludes recent GL entries — both nominally closed fast but left the team relying on manual Excel checks ("we're used to checking the underlying figures separately at this point"). Heading into contract renewal the customer is cutting seats from twelve to eight and states the reason explicitly: reporting moved to Excel "given the alert and dashboard issues from earlier this year" — a direct, textual link between reliability failures and reduced commitment ahead of renewal.

A light, well-spaced mix of setup questions and one bug report (a formula error) over a year, all resolved quickly and calmly, including proactive asks about auditor access and new data sources. A healthy, engaged account.

A genuine crisis point in mid-2025 — a 25-day export fix, then "the third serious outage in seven months" with the customer explicitly "reviewing whether Kataja can support our reporting cycle at all if this continues" — was followed by a colleague's escalation demanding a senior call before a board deadline. The team held the call and the fixes stuck: five subsequent tickets (August through October) are calm to enthusiastic ("really pleased with how stable things have been"), planning ahead for year-end exports, confirming genuine recovery rather than a lull.

A light, calm mix of a feature question left open (conditional formatting on calculated columns, never answered in the data) and two minor dashboard tickets resolved without complaint. Low volume, low stakes, one loose thread but no sign of dissatisfaction.
A single feature question about nested report sections, resolved without complaint. Too sparse to show a pattern, but nothing negative present.
